title: Rhythm checklist and ask scripting for manager sync
content:
Context: quick personal reference for weekly manager 1:1s. Goal is to keep conversations actionable, demonstrate signal (small, repeatable evidence), and surface blockers early. Use this as a living checklist and script bank.

Top outcomes I want from these syncs:
- Clarity on priority tradeoffs for next 6 weeks (which hires, which process work, which off-cycle org asks).
- One clear ask I can take away with a decision or next step (no vague promises).
- Feedback on top two behaviors I'm trying to build (e.g., delegation cadence; influencing cross-functional).

Three-minute framing (for opening):
- 30s (status): "High level: hiring pipeline stable; running two experiments to speed up interview loops; need guidance on reprioritizing L4 IC hiring vs L5 manager hire."
- 90s (evidence): quick bullets with metrics: time-to-offer down 12% M/M, interview no-shows 9% -> experiment A: hire admin for scheduling (pilot week 1). Link: JIRA-OPS-421.
- 60s (ask): "Recommend greenlight for pilot admin (1 month, $6k). If not greenlit, request guidance on which role to deprioritize."

One-minute elevator ask (if short on time):
- "I need approval to pilot a scheduling admin for one month to reduce no-shows and recruiter time sink; expected impact: recover 3 hours/week per recruiter and shorten time-to-offer ~10%. Can I move forward?"

Three-point priority ask template (use this for manager follow-up emails):
1) What I need: succinct ask + why (impact + metric)
2) Decision window: when I need an answer by
3) Fallback plan: what I'll do if answer is no

Quick evidence snippets to surface (micro-evidence style):
- Data point: "3 recruiters reported spending avg 5.8 hrs/week on scheduling (sample: last 2 weeks)"
- User quote: "Candidates said scheduling delays made us feel less responsive" (Slack #recruiting thread, 2026-02-10)
- Outcome projection: "Conservative estimate: 12 candidate touches saved / month -> 1 offer faster per 2 months"

Open blockers to bring up (short bullets):
- Budget cadence: where do pilot hires get approved for Q2? (Finance window vs hiring committee).
- Roadmap misalignment: product roadmap shifting interview demand by +30% in April; need to lock hiring commit.

Experiment plan (6 week):
- Week 0: pilot kickoff + 2 recruiters partner; logging time-savings (sheet: /people-ops/pilot-logs).
- Week 2: interim check-in with manager (15m) -> share raw time logs and candidate NPS.
- Week 4: adjust scope or scale down based on data.
- Week 6: decision and handoff.

Behavioral asks I want feedback on (prompt manager):
- "Am I delegating clear ownership or still holding too tightly?"
- "Do my sync notes produce clear decisions or ambiguous follow-ups?"

Prep checklist before sync: (tick box style, read aloud)
- 3 bullet status update (2 lines each)
- 1 concrete ask + decision window
- 1 supporting data point (metric or quote)
- 1 short escalation item if needed

Follow-up template (post-sync email, 30s to write):
- Subject: Recap + Decision Needed: [ask short title]
- Body: 1 sentence recap; 1 line decision requested + deadline; 1 line fallback; attach 1 supporting doc link.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep asks binary where possible (approve/decline or pick A/B).
- Track manager responses in a single thread to build signal over time (searchable).
- If manager is noncommittal twice, escalate to written ask with options.

Unresolved questions to bring up next:
- What is the default budget owner for short-term ops pilots under $10k? (Finance vs People Ops)
- Are we comfortable moving one L5 hire from H2 to H1 if pipeline risk materializes?

Quick links + refs (bookmark):
- Pilot logs sheet: https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/1PilotLogs
- Slack thread (scheduling pain): https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C03RECRUIT/p1686102340000
- Confluence: PROD-people-ops-rhythm

End note: keep this doc minimal and actionable; prune after each sync (archive old asks).
